Metadata refers to information that is not strictly required in order to run 
a study but is used to annotate the data within it. Succinctly, metadata is
data about data. Variable and value labels are examples of perhaps one 
of the most commonly used metadata in a study.

The recodeflow library aims to enable its users to include as much metadata 
as deemed necessary into the recoded dataset while also providing support for 
commonly used metadata fields like variable and value labels mentioned 
above. The next few sections goes through the scope and requirements of the
library from a metadata perspective.

## Variable metadata

As the name suggests, variable metadata refers to metadata that is used to 
annotate a variable and the values that it contains. 

All variable metadata used by the library is currently stored in the variable 
and variable details sheets. Both sheets are CSV files and use a pre-defined 
set of columns that the library recognizes and supports. This does not preclude 
users from adding additional columns for any custom metadata that 
they may want to include. Using a CSV file which is an open standard that is
supported by popular spreadsheet programs like Excel allows non-R users to contribute 
and make changes to the metadata. At the same time, making the sheet machine 
actionable by standardizing its structure allows the metadata to be easily read
and used by software.

The recodeflow library currently uses these sheets as the source of truth for 
all variable metadata and should continue to do so. As much as possible, any 
new metadata that the library wishes to support should be added to the sheets 
rather than for example being hardcoded in the library.

## Dataset metadata

Dataset metadata sits on top of variable metadata and is used to annotate an 
entire dataset and study. This can include information like the title of the 
study, the researchers involved in it, the study start date etc.

The library currently does not but should support this type of metadata. Existing 
standards should be adopted/extended like
`Dublin Core` or `DCAT`. In keeping with the theme of the rest of the library, 
any metadata standard chosen should be encoded in an open and machine actionable 
format to enable non-R and R users alike to use the information.

The library should allow users to import and annotate their dataset with the 
metadata. 

## Data dictionary

A data dictionary is a document that gives its readers information about a 
particular dataset like a description, how it should be used, the variables
contained within it, 
how they were derived etc. It is the first resource that users look to 
when exploring a dataset, acting as both an introduction and a reference
document.

The library should enable users to easily create a data dictionary including 
information from the variable and dataset metadata mentioned above.
### Metadata Schema Architecture

To support the metadata requirements outlined above, recodeflow implements 
a YAML-based schema architecture that:

- **Defines structure**: Formal specifications for variable and variable_details 
  CSV files including column names, types, constraints, and validation rules
- **Enables validation**: Schema-driven validation ensures data quality before 
  processing
- **Supports extensibility**: Project-specific metadata sections allow custom 
  fields while maintaining core compatibility
- **Facilitates interoperability**: LinkML-ready structure enables future 
  integration with semantic web standards and metadata exchange
- **Provides documentation**: Schemas serve as both machine specifications 
  and human documentation

This architecture ensures that metadata remains the "source of truth" as 
specified, while providing the structure needed for reliable software 
implementation.

For detailed specifications of the YAML metadata schemas, see 
[Metadata Schema Specifications](metadata-schemas.qmd).
